facts.statement: A proposition is a statement that is either true or false.
The law of noncontradiction states that contradictory statements cannot both be true in the same sense at the same time.
The law of excluded middle states that for any proposition, either that proposition is true or its negation is true.
Modus ponens is a rule of inference that infers Q from P and if P then Q.
Modus tollens infers not P from not Q and if P then Q.
A tautology is a logical formula that is true under every interpretation.
A contradiction is a logical formula that is false under every interpretation.
The negation of a conjunction is logically equivalent to the disjunction of the negations.
An argument is valid if the conclusion follows logically from the premises.
A set is a collection of distinct elements.
The empty set contains no elements.
The union of two sets contains all elements that belong to either set.
The intersection of two sets contains all elements that belong to both sets.
A subset is a set whose elements are all contained in another set.
Natural numbers are positive whole numbers beginning with 1.
Whole numbers include zero and the natural numbers.
Integers include positive whole numbers, negative whole numbers, and zero.
Rational numbers are numbers that can be expressed as a fraction of two integers.
Irrational numbers cannot be expressed as a fraction of two integers.
Real numbers include all rational and irrational numbers.
Prime numbers have exactly two distinct positive divisors.
Composite numbers have more than two positive divisors.
The number one is neither prime nor composite.
Two is the smallest prime number.
Even numbers are divisible by two.
Odd numbers are not divisible by two.
A square of a number is the number multiplied by itself.
A square root of a number is a value that when multiplied by itself equals the original number.
An exponent indicates how many times a base is multiplied by itself.
The order of operations in arithmetic is parentheses, exponents, multiplication and division, addition and subtraction.
Addition is commutative.
Multiplication is commutative.
Subtraction is not commutative.
Division is not commutative.
Zero added to any number equals that number.
One multiplied by any number equals that number.
Any number multiplied by zero equals zero.
Division by zero is undefined.
The decimal system uses base ten.
Binary uses base two.
A fraction represents a part of a whole.
A percentage is a fraction with denominator 100.
A ratio compares two quantities.
A proportion states that two ratios are equal.
An equation states that two expressions are equal.
An inequality compares two expressions using greater than or less than.
The square of the hypotenuse of a right triangle equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
The area of a rectangle equals its length multiplied by its width.
The perimeter of a rectangle is the sum of all its side lengths.
The area of a triangle equals one half times its base times its height.
The circumference of a circle equals pi times its diameter.
The area of a circle equals pi times the square of its radius.
A right angle measures 90 degrees.
A straight angle measures 180 degrees.
The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180 degrees.
A square has four equal sides and four right angles.
A rectangle has four right angles.
A parallelogram has opposite sides that are parallel.
A rhombus has four equal sides.
A circle is the set of all points in a plane at a fixed distance from a center.
The diameter of a circle is twice its radius.
Pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.
An isosceles triangle has at least two equal sides.
An equilateral triangle has three equal sides.
A scalene triangle has no equal sides.
Congruent figures have the same shape and size.
Similar figures have the same shape but not necessarily the same size.
A polygon is a closed plane figure with straight sides.
A quadrilateral has four sides.
A pentagon has five sides.
A hexagon has six sides.
A heptagon has seven sides.
An octagon has eight sides.
A decagon has ten sides.
A dodecagon has twelve sides.
Matter has mass and occupies space.
Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object.
Weight is the force of gravity acting on an object.
Density equals mass divided by volume.
Volume measures the amount of space an object occupies.
Energy is the capacity to do work.
Kinetic energy is the energy of motion.
Potential energy is stored energy due to position or condition.
The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed.
In a closed system, total energy remains constant.
Force equals mass times acceleration.
For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
An object at rest stays at rest unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.
An object in motion stays in motion with constant velocity unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
Velocity describes speed with direction.
Speed is the distance traveled per unit of time.
Friction opposes motion between two surfaces in contact.
Gravity is a force that attracts objects with mass toward one another.
On Earth, the acceleration due to gravity is approximately 9.8 meters per second squared.
Light travels in straight lines in a uniform medium.
The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792,458 meters per second.
Sound is a mechanical wave that requires a medium to travel.
Light is a form of electromagnetic radiation.
Heat is energy transferred between objects due to temperature difference.
Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of particles in a substance.
Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius under standard atmospheric pressure.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius under standard atmospheric pressure.
Solids have a definite shape and definite volume.
Liquids have a definite volume but take the shape of their container.
Gases have neither a definite shape nor a definite volume.
Plasma is a state of matter consisting of ionized gas.
Evaporation is the change of a liquid to a gas.
Condensation is the change of a gas to a liquid.
Melting is the change of a solid to a liquid.
Freezing is the change of a liquid to a solid.
Sublimation is the change of a solid directly to a gas.
An element is a substance made of only one type of atom.
A compound is a substance made of two or more elements chemically combined.
A mixture is a physical combination of two or more substances.
An atom is the basic unit of a chemical element.
A molecule is a group of atoms bonded together.
A proton has a positive electric charge.
An electron has a negative electric charge.
A neutron has no electric charge.
Protons and neutrons are located in the nucleus of an atom.
Electrons orbit the nucleus of an atom.
The atomic number of an element equals the number of protons in its nucleus.
The periodic table organizes chemical elements by atomic number.
A chemical reaction rearranges atoms to form new substances.
In a chemical reaction, mass is conserved.
An acid has a pH less than 7 in aqueous solution.
A base has a pH greater than 7 in aqueous solution.
A neutral solution has a pH of 7.
Water is a compound with the chemical formula H2O.
Carbon dioxide is a compound with the chemical formula CO2.
Oxygen is a chemical element with symbol O.
Hydrogen is the lightest chemical element.
Salt is a compound formed from the reaction of an acid and a base.
The Earth orbits the Sun.
The Moon orbits the Earth.
The Sun is a star.
The Earth is the third planet from the Sun.
The solar system includes the Sun and the objects that orbit it.
A planet is a celestial body that orbits a star.
A moon is a natural satellite that orbits a planet.
A galaxy is a large system of stars, gas, and dust held together by gravity.
The Milky Way is the galaxy that contains our solar system.
A light-year is the distance light travels in one year.
The speed of light is approximately 300,000 kilometers per second in a vacuum.
A day on Earth is the time it takes Earth to rotate once on its axis.
A year on Earth is the time it takes Earth to orbit the Sun once.
Earth rotates on its axis from west to east.
The tilt of Earth's axis causes seasons.
The Moon reflects light from the Sun.
A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth.
A lunar eclipse occurs when Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon.
A constellation is a group of stars that forms a recognizable pattern.
The force of gravity keeps planets in orbit around the Sun.
Stars produce energy through nuclear fusion.
A comet is a small icy body that releases gas and dust when near the Sun.
An asteroid is a rocky body that orbits the Sun.
A meteoroid is a small rocky or metallic body in space.
The universe contains all matter, energy, and space.
A telescope is an instrument used to observe distant objects.
An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined steps for solving a problem.
A program is a set of instructions that a computer can execute.
A programming language is a formal language used to write computer programs.
A variable is a named storage location in a computer program.
A constant is a value that does not change during program execution.
A function is a reusable block of code that performs a specific task.
A loop is a programming construct that repeats a block of code.
A conditional statement executes code based on whether a condition is true.
An array is a data structure that stores a collection of elements in a sequence.
A string is a sequence of characters.
An integer is a whole number data type.
A logical value is either true or false.
A compiler translates source code written in a high-level language into machine code.
An interpreter executes source code directly without producing a separate machine code file.
Source code is the human-readable text of a computer program.
Machine code is the lowest-level representation of a program executed by a computer.
A computer processes data using a central processing unit.
Random access memory stores data temporarily while a computer is running.
A hard disk drive stores data persistently.
An operating system manages computer hardware and software resources.
A file is a named collection of data stored on a computer.
A database is an organized collection of data.
A table in a relational database stores data in rows and columns.
A primary key uniquely identifies each record in a database table.
A query is a request for data from a database.
HTML is a markup language used to structure web pages.
CSS is a stylesheet language used to describe the presentation of a document.
The internet is a global network of interconnected computers.
The World Wide Web is a system of interlinked hypertext documents accessed via the internet.
A URL is a reference that specifies the location of a resource on the internet.
Binary code uses combinations of 0 and 1 to represent data.
A bit is the smallest unit of digital data.
A byte commonly consists of eight bits.
Encryption transforms data into a form that hides its original meaning.
A bug is an error or flaw in a computer program.
Debugging is the process of finding and fixing errors in a program.
A data structure is a way of organizing data in a computer.
A stack is a data structure that follows last-in first-out order.
A queue is a data structure that follows first-in first-out order.
A tree is a hierarchical data structure with nodes connected by edges.
A graph is a data structure made of vertices and edges.
Recursion is a technique in which a function calls itself.
An operating system schedules tasks for execution by the CPU.
Open source software has source code that anyone can inspect and modify.
A command-line interface accepts text commands from a user.
Data classification groups data into categories based on shared characteristics.
A spreadsheet organizes data into rows and columns.
A CSV file stores tabular data as comma-separated values.
Metadata is data that describes other data.
A data type defines the kind of value a variable can hold.
Sorting arranges data in a specified order.
Filtering selects a subset of data based on criteria.
A report presents data in a structured format for reading.
A backup is a copy of data made to protect against loss.
Data validation checks whether data meets specified requirements.
A relational database uses tables to store related data.
Normalization reduces data redundancy in a database.
A data model describes how data is structured and related.
An index in a database improves the speed of data retrieval.
A transaction is a unit of work performed within a database.
A sentence is a group of words that expresses a complete thought.
A noun names a person, place, thing, or idea.
A verb describes an action, occurrence, or state of being.
An adjective modifies a noun or pronoun.
An adverb modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb.
A pronoun takes the place of a noun.
A preposition shows the relationship between a noun or pronoun and another word.
A conjunction connects words, phrases, or clauses.
A period ends a declarative sentence.
A question mark ends an interrogative sentence.
A comma separates items in a list.
A paragraph is a group of related sentences.
A topic sentence states the main idea of a paragraph.
An outline organizes ideas hierarchically before writing.
A thesis statement presents the main argument of an essay.
A summary condenses the main points of a text.
A paraphrase restates a text in different words while preserving meaning.
A citation gives credit to a source used in writing.
A bibliography lists sources consulted for a research project.
The alphabet is a set of letters used to represent the sounds of a language.
A project is a temporary effort with a defined beginning and end.
A project has a goal or set of objectives.
A task is a piece of work assigned to a person or team.
A milestone is a significant point or event in a project.
A deadline is a date or time set for the completion of a task.
A schedule lists tasks and their planned start and end dates.
A dependency exists when one task cannot start until another task finishes.
A project schedule can be displayed as horizontal bars.
A stakeholder is a person or group with an interest in a project.
A deliverable is a tangible or intangible product produced by a project.
Scope describes the work required to complete a project.
A risk is an uncertain event that could affect a project.
A project plan documents how a project will be executed and controlled.
A budget estimates the financial resources needed for a project.
A project manager leads a project team.
A project phase is a distinct stage in a project lifecycle.
Time management is the process of planning and controlling how time is spent.
A calendar is a system for organizing days and events.
A to-do list lists tasks that need to be completed.
Prioritization ranks tasks by importance or urgency.
A time audit records how time is actually spent.
A timer tracks elapsed time for a specific activity.
A schedule allocates time to tasks and events.
Procrastination is the act of delaying a task.
A routine is a sequence of actions followed regularly.
A goal is a desired result that a person plans to achieve.
A deadline creates a time boundary for completing work.
A planner is a tool for recording appointments and tasks.
Active recall is a study technique that involves retrieving information from memory.
Spaced repetition reviews information at increasing intervals.
Note-taking records key information from a lecture or reading.
Summarizing condenses information into a shorter form.
A mnemonic is a memory aid.
A concept map shows relationships among ideas.
Practice testing improves retention of learned material.
A study schedule allocates specific times for studying.
Reading comprehension is the ability to understand written text.
Critical thinking is the objective analysis of facts to form a judgment.
A study group is a small group of people who study together.
A reference book provides facts and information on a subject.
A decimal classification system for libraries organizes books by subject.
A bibliographic record contains information that describes a library resource.
A catalog is a systematic list of library resources.
An index lists topics and page numbers in a book.
A table of contents lists the chapters or sections of a book.
A bibliography is a list of sources on a particular topic.
An abstract summarizes the content of a larger work.
A periodical is a publication issued at regular intervals.
A reference work is a book or digital resource consulted for factual information.
Classification groups items by shared characteristics.
A call number identifies the location of a library item.
Taxonomy is the science of classifying organisms.
The hierarchical levels in biological classification include kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species.
A species is a basic unit of biological classification.
A genus is a rank above species in biological classification.
Binomial nomenclature gives each species a two-part scientific name.
Living organisms are classified into domains and kingdoms.
Animals are multicellular organisms that typically consume other organisms.
Plants are multicellular organisms that typically produce their own food through photosynthesis.
Fungi are organisms that absorb nutrients from their environment.
